title: Tenant-aware Burst Capacity PRD and Launch Safety Checklist
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Enable controlled, tenant-scoped burst capacity for hosted inference endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) so teams can absorb short traffic spikes without outsized cost or cross-tenant impact. This feature provides per-tenant burst quotas, fair-share shaping, and automated fallbacks to cost-optimized variants while preserving latency SLOs for paying tiers. It targets production-hosted customers that need predictable economics with occasional burst traffic.
background:
Problem statement:
1) Customers experience unpredictable per-token cost during short spikes; either their traffic is throttled aggressively, or platform scales and increases unit cost for other tenants.
2) Current global autoscaling lacks per-tenant isolation and can cause noisy-neighbor latency regressions.
3) Sales and CS have asked for a formally supported per-tenant burst model that can be purchased (burst add-on) or enabled for higher tiers.
Why now:
- Dedicated pools are expensive for many customers; a hosted burst model balances cost/performance.
- Recent incidents highlighted cross-tenant degradation during spikes.
- Billing/usage infra is mature enough to attribute cost and enable per-tenant quotas.
goals:
1) Deliver a tenant-aware burst capability for hosted endpoints covering chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank within runtime-2.4.
2) Provide configurable burst quotas and decay policies per tenant.
3) Ensure latency SLOs for paying tiers (P95 latency targets) remain within 1.2x baseline during bursts.
4) Expose cost/usage visibility in Console and billing reports for burst consumption.
5) Ship rollout playbook and gating metrics to prevent cross-tenant regressions.
non_goals:
1) This PRD does not add new consumption billing models (e.g., per-burst-metered pricing); pricing will be negotiated separately but visible in billing.
2) Not covering Dedicated or Private runtime changes beyond routing hooks.
3) Not a general per-tenant capacity reservation (reserved capacity is handled by Dedicated offering).
requirements:
Core functional requirements:
- Per-tenant burst window definition: configurable in console (tokens/minute burst quota, burst duration, cool-down).
- Fair-share algorithm: ensure global CPU/GPU resources are shared proportionally under contention.
- Auto-fallback policies: when tenant burst is exhausted, route to a lower-cost model variant or enforce throttling based on configured policy.
- Endpoint compatibility: must work with chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank; support streaming for chat/completions.
- Telemetry: emit tenant-level metrics for burst usage, costs, latency percentiles, error counts.
- Billing: mark burst consumption in billing records for reconciliation.
- Admin controls: operator override, emergency pause, and tenant list for soft-rollouts.
- Safety: security_review_required flag enabled; no change to data isolation model.
- Observability: pre-built dashboards and alerts for cross-tenant tail latency regressions and cost anomalies.
endpoint_specific_requirements:
Chat:
- Maintain streaming semantics. Prefix caching behavior must be preserved across burst routing changes.
- P95 token latency target: baseline_p95 * 1.2 during bursts.
Completions:
- Support long-sequence workloads with KV cache hints; restrict burst window on sequences > 2048 tokens.
Embeddings:
- Burst policy keyed by vector requests per minute; ensure batch sizing logic honors tenant priority.
Rerank:
- Maintain deterministic ordering guarantees under fallback; if model variant has different scoring, annotate response with variant metadata for auditing.
acceptance_criteria:
MUST pass before GA:
1) E2E load test: simulate 500 tenants with 1% of tenants sending 10x baseline traffic; under configured burst quotas we observe: no more than 5% increase in cross-tenant P95 latency vs baseline; error rate < 0.5%.
2) Billing traceability: burst consumption appears as a distinct line-item in billing exports for each tenant.
3) Console: UI to configure burst quotas per tenant present in Console beta; telemetry widgets show real-time burst usage.
4) Rollback: an operator-initiated pause disables bursting within 60s and returns routing to pre-burst baseline.
5) Security review: threat model updated and sign-off from Security.
6) Integration tests: correctness of fallback routes across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank validated (including stream reconnect behavior for chat).
7) Documentation: PRD-derived public docs and pricing notes available in Confluence/Docs site.
8) Customer pilot: 2 pilot customers confirm SLA behavior under controlled blast tests.
9) Post-launch metric: cost-per-token delta for non-burst tenants remains within 2% of pre-launch baseline after 2 weeks of GA traffic.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal alpha): enable feature flag for platform and infra teams; smoke tests (2/week).
Phase 1 (private pilot): invite 2 customers in QA region; controlled spike exercises and billing validation.
Phase 2 (canary): 5% of hosted traffic in single region with monitoring and operator on-call; 48h observation window with gating metrics.
Phase 3 (gradual GA): region-by-region expansion with 24h evaluation windows; default off for new tenants, opt-in in Console.
Operator runbook highlights:
- Pause bursting: operator endpoint and expected rollback steps.
- Mitigation: route high-cost tenants to model-variant with quantized weights when under global contention.
- Escalation ladder: on-call SRE -> Infra PM -> Head of Runtime.
telemetry_and_observability:
Required dashboards and alerts:
- Tenant burst consumption heatmap by region/time.
- Cross-tenant P95/P99 latency delta vs baseline.
- Burst credit exhaustion events per tenant.
- Billing export ingestion success/failure.
- Anomaly alert: >10% of tenants experiencing latency regression for >15m.
Telemetry events to emit:
- burst.request_granted, burst.request_denied, burst.fallback_triggered, burst.exhausted, burst.pause_triggered.
SLOs to monitor:
- P95 latency targets per endpoint per tier.
- Error rate per tenant during burst windows.
- Billing reconciliation correctness (daily).
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Noisy-neighbor behavior still possible if fair-share misconfigured. Mitigation: conservative default burst quotas + canary.
Risk: Billing mismatches between burst and normal usage. Mitigation: parallel billing export validation in pilot.
Risk: Streaming complexity introduces session-affinity issues during fallback. Mitigation: session pinning and reconnect strategy for chat with transparent metadata to clients.
Risk: Complexity increases operational toil. Mitigation: operator tooling (pause, audit) and runbook automation.
dependencies:
- Runtime: kernel routing hooks and per-request tenant metadata tagging (ENG-22411).
- Billing: line-item tagging and export schema updates (ENG-31722).
- Console: UI for configuring burst quotas and telemetry widgets (DES-9080, ENG-40201).
- Security: threat model review and KMS usage verification (SEC-1203).
- Eval: create load profiles representative of target customers (RESEARCH-430).

notes:
Design trade-offs considered:
- Option A: Strict tenant reservations – simpler guarantees but expensive and low utilization.
- Option B (chosen): Soft guarantees + fair-share shaping – higher utilization, more complex routing.
Open questions:
- Should burst be enabled by default for paying tiers? (recommended: opt-in for safety).
- Pricing model: flat burst add-on vs metered—sales to confirm.
- How to mark response metadata in minimal spec without breaking clients? Use response header/JSON envelope.
